newsitem.title: UK: Euro straight-run fuel sought after but supply thin.
newsitem.headline: Euro straight-run fuel sought after but supply thin.

text.p: European straight-run fuel oil was eagerly sought on Tuesday but most would-be buyers were disappointed by thin supply levels, traders said.
Crude's sharp near $2 rise in the last week has destroyed refinery margins, leaving low sulphur straight-run a profitable alternative feedstock.

Two deals were seen yesterday, for 25,000 tonnes from Scandinavia at between $101 and $103 to a European major and for 30,000 tonnes from Antwerp to top up a cargo going to a U.S. refiner for $103 fob.
Offer levels climbed to $105 a tonne, or higher for premium quality fuel oil, with sellers complaining their material was still undervalued in relation to crude, which has hit two-month highs.
But very little material was believed available until the start of next month in north-west Europe.
Straight-run's price-hike has not been passed on yet to Russian material, traders said, which is in very short supply.
"Exporting just doesn't work for the Russians at the moment, price-wise, we'll have to see what happens later in the month," said one trader.
A flood of Russian fuel oil is expected on the European market later in the month once the summer inland barge traffic starts properly.
